title: Adaptive Compliance Intake Orchestrator for Security Questionnaires and DPA Negotiations
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Enterprise customers frequently submit long security questionnaires, DPAs, and audit requests that require manual triage across Legal, Security, and Engineering. Current intake is noisy: duplicate asks, inconsistent SLAs, and poor visibility for sales and CSMs. Goal: Build an orchestrator that ingests questionnaires and compliance requests, automatically classifies items (controls vs information vs contractual), estimates response effort and SLA, routes work to the right internal lane (Legal review, SOC2 evidence pack, infra remediation, or standard answers), and surfaces a prioritized worklist to PMs/SEs with clear owner, ETA, and evidence links. The feature must reduce manual triage time, improve SLA transparency for customers, and reduce duplicate work across deals.
acceptance_criteria: Classifier correctly labels >=85% of incoming questionnaire items into predefined buckets (Control, Evidence, Contractual Clause, Out-of-Scope) on a 200-item validation set.
Automated SLA estimator produces an initial ETA and owner for 90% of new intake items; 95% of items show a suggested route (Legal / Security SME / Engineering / Standard Answers).
Integration events emitted to CRM (Salesforce) and ticketing (Jira) for routed items with metadata (customer, applicable control, estimated ETA).
UI: Triage queue in Console displays priority, estimated ETA, customer impact score, and one-click create-to-ticket flow.
Operational: Metrics dashboard with triage time, SLA adherence, and duplicate-detection rate; initial alert when backlog > 48 hours for high-impact customers.
Privacy: No customer PII is stored unencrypted; access controls enforce RBAC for evidence artifacts.
scope: Phase 1: Ingest CSV/Word/PDF questionnaires and attachments; basic NLP classifier and rule-based fallback; routing to Legal/Security/Engineering lanes.
Phase 2: SLA estimator tuned on historical ticket durations, duplicate detection, auto-suggested evidence artifacts, and automated response templates for common asks.
Phase 3: Two-way integrations (Salesforce/Jira), customer-facing status page for active requests, and support for DPA clause negotiation tracking.
Out of scope: Full contract redlining automation; audit remediation automation beyond evidence collection.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Classifier accuracy initially limited by training data; mitigate by conservative routing and human-in-the-loop review for high-impact customers.
Over-automation risk: misrouted contractual clauses could create legal exposure — require Legal sign-off for any automated clause-level responses.
Operational cost: storing or indexing large evidence artifacts increases storage; prefer hashed manifests + links to secure object stores instead of copying full artifacts by default.
SLA estimator complexity: external dependencies (third-party vendors, customer responsiveness) reduce estimate reliability; show ranges and confidence scores instead of single-point ETAs.
milestones: 2026-03-15: Prototype classifier + routing demo to Security and Legal
2026-04-12: Console triage queue MVP + CRM webhooks
2026-04-26: Pilot with two enterprise customers (finance + healthcare), measure triage time
implementation_notes: Start with a hybrid approach: off-the-shelf NLP model for semantic mapping, plus domain-specific rule overrides maintained by Legal/Security.
Expose a triage feedback loop: allow SMEs to reclassify items and persist corrections to improve model over time.
Store evidence manifests in S3 with tenant-scoped prefixes and pointer metadata in Redwood Console; use KMS-wrapped keys per customer for high-sensitivity artifacts.
Provide a low-friction create-ticket flow from Console to Jira with prepopulated metadata and suggested assignee.
rollout_plan: Pilot with 2 high-touch accounts for 4 weeks; collect quantitative metrics and qualitative SME feedback.
Iterate on classifier rules and SLA estimator based on pilot data, then expand to 10 accounts for closed beta.
Public beta: expose feature to Enterprise customers via Console toggle; include runbook and training docs for Sales/CS.
Full launch gated on 85% classifier performance and signed-off legal controls for automated responses.
metrics: Mean time to triage (target: <= 24 hours for high-impact customers)
Percent of items auto-classified correctly (target: >=85% after pilot)
Duplicate detection reduction (target: 30% fewer duplicate asks routed)
SLA adherence for routed items (target: 90% within estimated window)
